Words used here
conscious access
Information becoming available for such things as reporting or deliberately using it. Explaining this does not by itself explain all experience.
Read the fuller explanation

Change the canopy’s view. In one setting, one cluster is sharply available and the rest recedes. In another, the wider arrangement becomes legible. The illustration changes presentation; it does not measure your attention or assign you a type.

The functional atlas distinguishes readiness, sustained processing, vigilance, selective focus and divided allocation. It also separates these from conscious access, action and the experience of agency. A familiar word can compress several different operations.

The useful question is which transition is being explained, on which evidence, and what rival account remains. A diagram of a distributed system cannot by itself tell us what experience is. That unresolved join belongs in the clearing too.
